title: State Space Models for Realtime Multimodal Intelligence: Karan Goel
talk_summary: Karan Goel pitches state space models (Mamba lineage) as a streaming, compression-based alternative to Transformers for realtime multimodal inference, arguing quadratic attention is too expensive for long audio/video/sensor context. It is an architecture-research talk with no agent-orchestration, review, or workflow content.

takeaways.what_they_do: Argues models should compress incoming streams into a fixed internal state rather than keep all tokens and re-attend, claiming compression helps long-context tasks more than short ones.
takeaways.evidence_quote: compression can be helpful so if you imagine the security camera example if you're watching 24 hours of footage actually compressing all that information on the fly would help you solve tasks

takeaways.what_they_do: Claims Transformer attention scales quadratically with context so heavy long-context inference is economically unsustainable; SSMs scale more linearly.
